item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The first post sidetracked me over to 646 but Dr. Elderglass reminded me what I was going to say, lol!

I love when SCPs are inspired from real-life mythology, scenarios or stories. That being said, I feel as though this one, being based off a well-known mythos, is a little bland and dry for the usual reality-based SCPs. The background is actually good, including the Gaelic dialect and finding it in Ireland, all good concepts.

But aside from the acquisition log, I feel I want more. I feel as though this thing isn't just going to sit quietly, waiting for us to provide heat for it, while possessing the ability to, apparently, change the atmosphere, or at least the temperature, around it. It also, apparently…

…has exhibited the capability to cause considerable havoc when deprived of warmth.

I think this thing is worthy of at least one incident log, don't the rest of you?

But other than that it's decently well written, invokes creativity and again, as I said, is inspired from an already-established fiction. It's just not enough for me to affect the rating yet. Leaving it as it is. Oh, and, commendations for Agent ██████ anyone?

item.content:encoded: I agree with the others on here, this one shows great potential but in its current state is disappointingly lacking. I really think with a rewrite this one could be awesome. An idea that came to mind immediately upon reading it for me was that someone should actually write that log of conversation transcripts that's mentioned. That would be a good start I think. To continue, maybe turn it into some kind of ghost story or something, sort of like what the rewrite of 265 did with that stuff about the pond. Heck, one idea would maybe be to expand upon that thing with the Irish kids that found this one, maybe even tie the fact that it doesn't seem to be aware of the effect it has on people by turning it into some sort of tragic ghost story about a young child who doesn't even realize they're a ghost and just wants to be comforted or something along those lines.

It seems that most of the older SCPs are just anamlous things. They lack a narrative, and speak more like a report.
It's good to see the staff going through these old ones, as these SCP's will give the first impression of what's a good SCP to new people. This definitely raises the bar for expectations, since we're supposed to be writing with a story in mind for an item.
And I agree with Roget's statements, -1 for now.
